tools.name: list_channels
tools.description: List your channels. Every project lives in a channel, which owns the reusable styles (art/narrative/director) that drive generation.

tools.name: create_channel
tools.description: Create a new channel — the container for projects and their reusable styles. Use when the user wants a fresh creative identity rather than adding to an existing channel.

params.name: name
params.description: Display name for the new channel

params.name: description
params.description: Optional free-text description of the channel's content focus

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List projects in a channel.

params.name: channel_id
params.description: ID of the channel whose projects to list, from list_channels or create_channel

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project. The description (the video concept/topic) seeds script generation, so write a meaningful one. The response's web_url is the project's page in the web app — share it so the user can follow along.

params.name: title
params.description: Project title shown in the app

params.name: channel_id
params.description: ID of the channel to create the project in, from list_channels or create_channel

params.name: description
params.description: The video concept/topic; seeds script generation, so make it specific and meaningful

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Fetch a project row — settings, voice config, default style, export URL.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Patch project fields. Updatable: title, description, asset_mix, sfx_level, video_concept, voice_mix, voice_tts_provider, script_target_minutes, narrator_speed. (The narrator's TTS voice is NOT here — use set_narrator_voice.)

params.name: fields
params.description: Partial dict of fields to patch; allowed keys: title, description, asset_mix, sfx_level, video_concept, voice_mix, voice_tts_provider, script_target_minutes, narrator_speed

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Permanently delete a project and everything in it (script versions, assets, voiceover, segments, renders). Irreversible — confirm with your user first.

params.name: project_id
params.description: ID of the project to permanently delete, from list_projects

tools.name: set_project_style
tools.description: Set the project's default style — the style whose art/narrative/director fields drive its generations. Use after create_style to put a new visual identity into effect, or to switch a project between channel styles.

params.name: style_id
params.description: ID of the style to make the project's default, from create_style or list_styles

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: update_caption_config
tools.description: Merge a patch into the project's burned-in caption config (keys like enabled, plus styling). Read the current value from get_project (caption_config). Applies at the next export — no rebuild needed.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: caption_config
params.description: Partial caption config to merge (keys like enabled, plus styling); read the current value from get_project's caption_config

tools.name: get_pipeline_progress
tools.description: THE resume/orientation tool: one call returns every pipeline step's state (script -> scan -> reference_images -> voices -> voiceover -> style_templates -> storyboard -> segment_assets -> scenes -> export), any running jobs, and a next_action telling you exactly what to do next. Call this when picking up an existing project, after any await_jobs, or whenever you're unsure where a video stands — never guess pipeline position. Every step carries a web_url — the page in the Framesail web app where y

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: get_workflow_status
tools.description: Poll this between steps: returns active + recently-finished AI jobs (scope by project_id, or style_id for style analysis), plus per-segment- asset render statuses for projects. A step is done when its jobs reach status=complete (or error, with a user-readable message). NOTE: finished jobs drop out of `jobs` after ~30s — a short list does NOT mean work was lost; judge render batches by `segment_assets` statuses (or get_pipeline_progress), never by counting jobs. Prefer await_jobs over polling thi

params.name: style_id
params.description: Style ID to scope jobs to (style analysis); pass exactly one of project_id or style_id

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID to scope jobs to; pass exactly one of project_id or style_id

tools.name: await_jobs
tools.description: Block (server-side) until the scope has no pending/running jobs, or the timeout passes — use this instead of polling get_workflow_status yourself. Returns {done, jobs}. If done=false the work is still running: just call await_jobs again (a 3-5 minute storyboard takes a few consecutive calls). Keep timeout_seconds <= 50 so the client doesn't time out the tool call.

params.name: style_id
params.description: Style ID whose analysis/template jobs to wait for; pass exactly one of project_id or style_id

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID whose jobs to wait for; pass exactly one of project_id or style_id

params.name: timeout_seconds
params.description: Max seconds to block server-side before returning done=false; keep <= 50 so the client doesn't time out the tool call

tools.name: get_section_template
tools.description: Inspect the prompt sections a generation job exposes for per-call override via editable_sections (jobs: script, script_scan, storyboard, segment_image, segment_video, voice_block, ...). Sections marked locked cannot be overridden.

params.name: job
params.description: Generation job name, e.g. "script", "script_scan", "storyboard", "segment_image", "segment_video", "voice_block"

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the models allowed for a generation job, with display names, credit estimates, and each model's settings_schema — the valid keys for that tool's `settings` param (e.g. image quality/orientation, video duration). The first entry is the default every tool uses when model is omitted.

params.name: job
params.description: Generation job whose allowed models to list, e.g. "script", "storyboard", "segment_image", "segment_video", "voice_block"

tools.name: generate_script
tools.description: Generate the project's script from its description/concept and the channel's narrative style. Async — returns {job_id}; poll get_workflow_status.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ID to generate with; empty uses the default (see list_models("script"))

params.name: settings
params.description: Model-specific settings; valid keys come from the model's settings_schema in list_models("script")

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides, keyed by section name; see get_section_template("script") for the sections this job exposes

tools.name: get_script
tools.description: Read the active script's full text + the version list. Use this to show the script to your user for review/feedback before scan_script — the review-edit-resave loop (get_script -> discuss -> save_script) is the expected workflow when the user wants input.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: save_script
tools.description: Save script text (your own draft, or an edited version of the generated one — saving creates a new version, old versions are kept). Run scan_script afterwards so assets and voice blocks reflect the new text.

params.name: content
params.description: Full script text to save as a new version; plain prose narration, optionally with scene headings

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: revise_script
tools.description: AI-rewrite a passage of the active script in the project's narrative voice (the same in-editor revise the UI offers). selected_text must appear verbatim in the script; omit it to revise the whole script. Synchronous — returns {revised_text}, which is NOT saved: splice it over selected_text (or replace the full script) and call save_script to keep it.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: instruction
params.description: Natural-language edit instruction, e.g. "make the intro punchier"

params.name: selected_text
params.description: Exact passage to rewrite; must appear verbatim in the active script. Omit to revise the whole script

tools.name: activate_script_version
tools.description: Switch the project's active script to another saved version (ids come from get_script's version list — every save_script creates one). Re-run scan_script / rescan_voice_blocks afterwards if the text differs, since downstream artifacts follow the active version.

params.name: script_id
params.description: ID of the script version to activate, from get_script's version list

tools.name: scan_script
tools.description: Analyze the active script: extracts character/environment/object assets and splits narration into voice blocks. DESTRUCTIVE on re-run (assets are recreated, not merged — curated descriptions, reference images, and voices are lost; prefer rescan_voice_blocks after script edits). Async — returns {job_id}.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ID to scan with; empty uses the default (see list_models("script_scan"))

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides, keyed by section name; see get_section_template("script_scan")

tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: List the project's assets extracted by scan_script — characters, environments, objects. Each has a description (the spec every shot uses to render it — surfaced top-level here; the raw row nests it at ai_output.description), an optional reference image (file_path is a public URL — view_image it), and for characters a voice_id. Review these after scan_script: fix descriptions, then generate_asset_reference for each one (all of them need a reference image before voiceover). asset_type filter: "cha

params.name: asset_type
params.description: Optional filter: "character", "environment", or "object"; empty lists all asset types

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: create_asset
tools.description: Manually add a character/environment/object the scan missed. asset_type: "character" | "environment" | "object". The description is the generation-facing spec of its look — be specific.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name as the script refers to it (e.g. the character's name)

params.name: asset_type
params.description: Kind of asset: "character", "environment", or "object"

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: description
params.description: Generation-facing spec of the asset's look; every shot renders from it, so be specific

tools.name: update_asset
tools.description: Rename an asset and/or rewrite its description. If the look changed, regenerate its reference image afterwards so renders match.

params.name: name
params.description: New asset name; empty leaves the name unchanged

params.name: asset_id
params.description: Asset ID, as returned by list_assets or create_asset

params.name: description
params.description: New generation-facing look description; empty leaves it unchanged

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Delete a project asset (e.g. one the scan over-extracted).

params.name: asset_id
params.description: ID of the asset to delete, from list_assets

tools.name: generate_asset_reference
tools.description: Render an asset's reference image in the channel's art style — the visual anchor that keeps a character/environment looking identical across every shot. EVERY character, environment, and object asset needs one before generate_voiceover (the server enforces this; fire the jobs for all assets, then one await_jobs). Async — the job writes the image onto the asset row: await_jobs(project_id), then list_assets and view_image the file_path to check likeness.

params.name: model
params.description: Image model ID; empty uses the server default for reference images

params.name: asset_id
params.description: ID of the asset to render a reference image for, from list_assets

params.name: settings
params.description: Model-specific settings (e.g. image quality/orientation); valid keys come from the model's settings_schema in list_models

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides, keyed by section name; see get_section_template for the reference-image job

tools.name: set_character_voice
tools.description: Bind a TTS voice to a character asset — required before generate_voiceover for every character with dialogue (the narrator's voice is separate: set_narrator_voice). Browse ids with list_voices.

params.name: asset_id
params.description: Character asset ID, from list_assets

params.name: voice_id
params.description: TTS voice ID, from list_voices (use the provider matching the project's voice_tts_provider)

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List available TTS voices (id, label, preview audio URL) for a provider: "minimax" (default engine) or "elevenlabs". Match the project's voice_tts_provider (see get_project) so picked ids work with its engine.

params.name: provider
params.description: TTS engine to list voices for: "minimax" (default engine) or "elevenlabs"; match the project's voice_tts_provider

tools.name: set_narrator_voice
tools.description: Set the project's narrator TTS voice — required before generate_voiceover whenever the script has narration. Browse ids with list_voices. (Character dialogue voices are separate: set_character_voice.)

params.name: voice_id
params.description: TTS voice ID for the narrator, from list_voices (use the provider matching the project's voice_tts_provider)

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: list_voice_blocks
tools.description: List the project's voice blocks (per-speaker narration chunks) with their audio status and assigned voices.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: update_voice_block
tools.description: Override one voice block's voice or playback volume (block ids from list_voice_blocks). Re-run generate_voiceover for the block afterwards if you changed its voice — existing audio is not regenerated automatically.

params.name: volume
params.description: Playback volume for this block, 0-1; omit to leave unchanged

params.name: voice_id
params.description: New TTS voice ID for this block, from list_voices; empty leaves the voice unchanged

params.name: voice_block_id
params.description: Voice block ID, from list_voice_blocks

tools.name: rescan_voice_blocks
tools.description: Re-extract voice blocks from the active script WITHOUT touching assets or their reference images — the non-destructive alternative to scan_script after a script edit. Existing audio is superseded by the new block split, so re-run generate_voiceover afterwards. Async — returns {job_id}.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ID for the re-extraction; empty uses the default (see list_models("voice_block_scan"))

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: generate_voiceover
tools.description: Generate TTS audio for the project's voice blocks. Without voice_block_ids it fills gaps: only blocks with no audio yet run, so re-calling it is always safe (already-generated and currently-generating blocks are skipped, never re-billed). Pass voice_block_ids to explicitly REgenerate those blocks (e.g. after changing a block's voice). Speakers must have voices bound first — set_narrator_voice / set_character_voice. Optional editable_sections/settings apply to every selected block (see get_sectio

params.name: model
params.description: TTS model ID; empty uses the default (see list_models("voice_block"))

params.name: settings
params.description: Model-specific TTS settings applied to every selected block; valid keys come from the model's settings_schema in list_models("voice_block")

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: voice_block_ids
params.description: Block IDs (from list_voice_blocks) to explicitly REgenerate; omit to fill gaps — only blocks with no audio yet run

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides applied to every selected block; see get_section_template("voice_block")

tools.name: generate_storyboard
tools.description: Plan the full visual storyboard: segments, shot pacing, image/video prompts, overlays, continuation chains — driven by the channel's director and art styles. Requires voiceover to exist (timing comes from it). BEFORE calling: confirm the project's asset_mix with your user (image vs video vs generated_graphic percentages, update_project) — the storyboard plans against it and video-heavy mixes multiply the later render cost. Async — returns {job_id}; this is the longest LLM step.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ID to plan with; empty uses the default (see list_models("storyboard"))

params.name: settings
params.description: Model-specific settings; valid keys come from the model's settings_schema in list_models("storyboard")

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides, keyed by section name; see get_section_template("storyboard")

tools.name: get_segments
tools.description: List the storyboard's segments (narration span, type, duration, creative direction). The 1-based segment_number is the handle every segment tool takes (update/split/combine/continuation/regenerate) — you never need a UUID. Each segment also reports `continues_from_segment`. When set, this shot is a CONTINUATION of that earlier segment: its rendered frame carries over (same composition, characters, and setting) and only the delta changes — an added overlay, a shifted expression, a closer angle, a

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: get_segment_assets
tools.description: List one segment's assets (images/video/overlays) including their status, config (prompts, model), and public URLs of rendered files — pass an image's public_url to view_image to actually look at it.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

tools.name: regenerate_segment_asset
tools.description: Regenerate a segment's primary image or video with optional overrides — the API equivalent of the editor's expert drawer. asset_type: "image" | "video" (for a video segment, "image" targets its start frame). Use a different model, override prompt sections (see get_section_template("segment_image")), or tweak settings (e.g. image quality), then re-run just this asset. Async — returns {job_id}.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ID to render with; empty uses the job's default (see list_models("segment_image") / list_models("segment_video"))

params.name: settings
params.description: Model-specific settings (e.g. image quality, video duration); valid keys come from the model's settings_schema in list_models

params.name: asset_type
params.description: "image" or "video"; for a video segment, "image" targets its start frame

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides, keyed by section name; see get_section_template("segment_image") or ("segment_video")

tools.name: change_segment_type
tools.description: Change a segment's visual type: "image" | "video" | "overlay_scene". carry_frame=true reuses the already-rendered image as the video start frame (or vice versa) instead of recreating it.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: carry_frame
params.description: True reuses the already-rendered frame as the new type's starting visual instead of recreating it from scratch

params.name: segment_type
params.description: New visual type: "image", "video", or "overlay_scene"

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

tools.name: update_segment_content
tools.description: Rewrite one segment's creative direction from feedback ("make this shot a close-up", "show the machine from above") — an LLM rewrites the shot's prompts; continuation links, SFX, and overlays are preserved. The visual assets reset to not_started: re-render them afterwards (generate_segments or regenerate_segment_asset). For a precise prompt tweak with no rewrite, use regenerate_segment_asset with editable_sections instead.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: user_input
params.description: Natural-language feedback describing the change to this shot, e.g. "make this a close-up" or "show the machine from above"

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

tools.name: split_segment
tools.description: Split a segment at the given time offsets (ms, 1-3 cuts → 2-4 parts). inherit_index picks which resulting part keeps the original creative data. Later segments renumber — re-check get_segments before further edits.

params.name: offsets_ms
params.description: Cut points as millisecond offsets from the segment start, ascending; 1-3 cuts producing 2-4 parts

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: inherit_index
params.description: 0-based index of the resulting part that keeps the original creative data (default: the first part)

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based number of the segment to split, as reported by get_segments

tools.name: combine_segments
tools.description: Merge a segment with an adjacent one (segment numbers must be neighbors). keep: "this" | "other" — whose creative data survives. Later segments renumber — re-check get_segments before further edits.

params.name: keep
params.description: Whose creative data survives the merge: "this" (segment_number) or "other" (with_segment_number)

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

params.name: with_segment_number
params.description: 1-based number of the adjacent segment to merge with (must neighbor segment_number)

tools.name: set_segment_continuation
tools.description: Make a segment's image render as a continuation of an EARLIER segment's frame (same composition evolving — the storyboard's continues_from_segment, settable after the fact). continues_from is that earlier segment's number; pass 0 to clear the link. Regenerate the segment's image afterwards — the reference is applied at generation time.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: continues_from
params.description: 1-based number of the EARLIER segment whose frame this one continues; pass 0 to clear the link

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based number of the segment whose image should continue an earlier frame, as reported by get_segments

tools.name: add_segment_sfx
tools.description: Attach a sound effect from the audio library to a segment (find track ids via browse_audio_library with category="sfx"). Re-run build_scenes to get it onto the timeline.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

params.name: library_track_id
params.description: Audio library track ID, from browse_audio_library(category="sfx")

tools.name: remove_segment_sfx
tools.description: Remove a sound effect from a segment. With one SFX attached, no name needed; with several, pass sfx_name (the asset name shown by get_segment_assets).

params.name: sfx_name
params.description: Name of the SFX asset to remove, as shown by get_segment_assets; needed only when the segment has several SFX attached

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: segment_number
params.description: 1-based segment number, as reported by get_segments

tools.name: generate_segments
tools.description: Render every actionable segment asset (images, video clips, overlays) across the project, in dependency order. THE most expensive call in the pipeline: ALWAYS dry_run=true first, show your user the estimate next to get_credit_balance, and wait for a fresh yes before the real run — prior blanket permission ("do the whole thing") does not cover this spend. Pass segment_numbers to render only a subset — e.g. segments 1-18 for the opening minute before committing to the full video. Safe to re-run: c

params.name: dry_run
params.description: True returns the credit-cost estimate without rendering anything; ALWAYS run true first and get user approval before the real run

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: segment_numbers
params.description: 1-based segment numbers (from get_segments) to render only a subset; omit to render every actionable asset in the project

tools.name: build_scenes
tools.description: Compile segments + assets + voiceover into the editor/render timeline (scenes). Run after segment assets are complete, before export.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: list_scenes
tools.description: List the project's scenes (composition layers, durations, layout).

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: director_note
tools.description: Edit ONE scene with a natural-language note (the same director chat the editor UI uses): move/restyle/add/remove layers and overlays, retime, etc. Synchronous — returns the applied mutations + updated scene. Use list_scenes to find scene ids; for notes spanning the whole video use project_director_note instead.

params.name: message
params.description: Natural-language edit note for this scene, e.g. "move the caption to the top" or "remove the overlay"

params.name: scene_id
params.description: ID of the scene to edit, from list_scenes

params.name: conversation_history
params.description: Prior chat turns as [{"role": ..., "content": ...}] to continue an editing conversation on this scene; omit to start fresh

tools.name: project_director_note
tools.description: Apply a project-WIDE director note ("make the intro punchier", "all captions bigger", "tighten pacing in the back half"). A routing pass picks only the scenes the note applies to and edits each one. Synchronous — a few seconds per affected scene. Returns the per-scene results; re-run export_video afterwards to see changes in the final render.

params.name: message
params.description: Project-wide director note in natural language, e.g. "make the intro punchier" or "all captions bigger"

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: export_video
tools.description: Render the final MP4 (Remotion). Fetches the current timeline and queues the render. Async — poll get_workflow_status for the video_export job, then call get_video_url.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: get_video_url
tools.description: Download URL for the most recent completed export.

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description: List the channel's style rows (variable groups). Styles hold the art_style / narrative_style / director_style / script_prompt fields that drive every generation step, plus any custom @variables.

params.name: channel_id
params.description: ID of the channel that owns the styles, from list_channels

tools.name: get_style
tools.description: Fetch one style row — its inputs (reference material) and analyzed fields (art_style, narrative_style, director_style, script_prompt, ...). Show fields to the user for review; fine-tune with update_style_fields.

params.name: style_id
params.description: Style ID, as returned by create_style or list_styles

tools.name: update_style_fields
tools.description: Hand-edit a style's analyzed fields after reviewing them — e.g. tighten the art_style wording or adjust the director_style pacing rules. `fields` is the FULL flat dict to write: {key: {"value": str, "applies_to": [...]}} (fetch with get_style, modify, send back). Editing fields does NOT trigger re-analysis, so your edits stick.

params.name: fields
params.description: FULL flat dict of analyzed fields to write, shaped {key: {"value": str, "applies_to": [...]}} — fetch with get_style, modify, send the whole dict back

params.name: style_id
params.description: Style ID, as returned by create_style or list_styles

tools.name: list_style_presets
tools.description: The curated preset catalog for the no-AI style creation path, grouped by axis (art_style / narrative_style / director_style). Show the user the labels + descriptions and let THEM pick one per axis — don't choose silently. Art presets include preview image URLs (view_image works on them). Create with create_style(presets={axis: id, ...}) — instant, no analysis job. Full field text lands on the style row (get_style shows it after creation).

tools.name: create_style
tools.description: Create a style. Two mutually exclusive paths: References (best): inputs=[{"input_type": "youtube" | "text", "value": "<url or description>"}] — YouTube videos are watched and text directions read; async analysis writes the style's art/narrative/director fields: await_jobs(style_id=...) before using the style. (Image/video FILE references require the multipart REST endpoint POST /styles.) Presets (instant, no analysis): presets={"art_style": id, "narrative_style": id, "director_style": id} — all

params.name: name
params.description: Display name for the style

params.name: inputs
params.description: Reference material to analyze, [{"input_type": "youtube" | "text", "value": "<url or description>"}]; triggers an async analysis job. Mutually exclusive with presets

params.name: presets
params.description: Preset IDs per axis, {"art_style": id, "narrative_style": id, "director_style": id}, from list_style_presets; instant, no analysis. Mutually exclusive with inputs

params.name: channel_id
params.description: ID of the channel to create the style in, from list_channels

tools.name: analyze_style
tools.description: Re-run style analysis (after changing a style's inputs). Async — await_jobs(style_id=...) until the style_analysis job completes.

params.name: style_id
params.description: ID of the style to re-analyze, from create_style or list_styles

tools.name: generate_style_template
tools.description: Render one of a style's two template images — a REAL step of style setup, not an optional extra: a style isn't finished until both its character and environment templates are rendered (the app shows them on the style card). Asset reference images render against them (characters → character template; environments and objects → environment template), and segment renders fall back on them when a shot has no asset reference — so finish BOTH before generate_asset_reference. Run once per template_type

params.name: model
params.description: Image model ID; empty uses the template job's default (see list_models)

params.name: style_id
params.description: Style ID, as returned by create_style or list_styles

params.name: template_type
params.description: Which of the style's two template images to render: "character" or "environment" — run once for each

params.name: editable_sections
params.description: Per-call prompt section overrides, keyed by section name; see get_section_template for the template job

tools.name: delete_style
tools.description: Delete a style (e.g. a failed analysis experiment). Don't delete a style that projects still use as their default — rebind them first with set_project_style.

params.name: style_id
params.description: ID of the style to delete, from list_styles

tools.name: set_provider_key
tools.description: Register a BYOK provider API key (encrypted at rest, BYOK plan only). Jobs whose model belongs to this provider then run on YOUR key and charge 0 credits. Providers: openai, gemini, anthropic, fal, elevenlabs, minimax.

params.name: key
params.description: The provider API key to register; stored encrypted at rest

params.name: provider
params.description: Provider the key belongs to: "openai", "gemini", "anthropic", "fal", "elevenlabs", or "minimax"

tools.name: list_provider_keys
tools.description: List registered BYOK providers (masked — only the last 4 characters).

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Verify the connection: the account email and plan behind the current credential. Call once after connecting — before creating anything — to confirm you're on the right account; costs nothing.

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description: Current credit balance + plan info. Check before expensive steps (a full segment render can cost hundreds of credits — generate_segments dry_run gives the estimate). Jobs covered by a BYOK provider key bill 0.

tools.name: browse_audio_library
tools.description: Browse the audio library for background music and sound effects. category: "music" | "sfx". Returns track ids for add_music_track / add_segment_sfx.

params.name: mood
params.description: Filter by the track's mood tag; empty for no filter

params.name: genre
params.description: Filter by the track's genre tag; empty for no filter

params.name: search
params.description: Free-text search over track names/descriptions; empty for no filter

params.name: category
params.description: Track kind: "music" (background tracks) or "sfx" (sound effects); empty returns both

tools.name: list_music_tracks
tools.description: List the project's background music tracks (volume, loop, timing).

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

tools.name: add_music_track
tools.description: Add background music to the project from the audio library (find track ids with browse_audio_library, category="music"). Defaults loop the track under the whole video at bed level (volume 0.2 ≈ -14 dB under narration — don't raise it without being asked); re-run export_video to hear it.

params.name: loop
params.description: True loops the track under the whole video; false plays it once

params.name: name
params.description: Display name for the track on the project's timeline

params.name: volume
params.description: Playback volume 0-1; the 0.2 default sits at bed level under narration — don't raise it unless asked

params.name: project_id
params.description: Project ID, as returned by create_project or list_projects

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Timeline frame at which the track starts (0 = start of the video)

params.name: library_track_id
params.description: Audio library track ID, from browse_audio_library(category="music")

tools.name: update_music_track
tools.description: Tweak a music track. fields keys: name, volume (0-1), loop, start_frame, duration_frames, position, trim_start_frame, trim_end_frame.

params.name: fields
params.description: Partial dict of track fields to patch; allowed keys: name, volume (0-1), loop, start_frame, duration_frames, position, trim_start_frame, trim_end_frame

params.name: track_id
params.description: Music track ID, from list_music_tracks or add_music_track

tools.name: remove_music_track
tools.description: Remove a music track from the project.

params.name: track_id
params.description: ID of the music track to remove, from list_music_tracks

tools.name: view_image
tools.description: Fetch a rendered Framesail image so you (and your user) can SEE it — pass a URL from get_segment_assets, get_style, or asset endpoints. Returns the image inline. Only Framesail media URLs are allowed.

params.name: url
params.description: Public Framesail media URL to fetch — a public_url from get_segment_assets, a file_path from list_assets, or a template/preset image URL from get_style / list_style_presets; other hosts are rejected
